Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
125 PM PST Fri Nov 20 2026

.SYNOPSIS...19/1001 PM.

Dry weather is expected through at least Sunday afternoon. Highs 
are will be around 5 degrees below normal. Overnight lows will be
chilly as well, with some areas dropping below freezing. Light 
rain is possible Sunday night into Monday and again next 
Wednesday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-MON)...20/124 PM.

For the short term period, latest models in good synoptic
agreement through the period. At upper levels, weak disturbance
will zip across the area this afternoon/evening with a weak
ridge building over the area on Saturday. For Sunday and Monday,
this upper ridge will give way to a weak trough moving across the
area. At the surface, weak offshore flow develop tonight and
Saturday with weak onshore flow returning on Sunday and Monday.

Forecast-wise, main "concern" in the short term will be the
chances of precipitation. With the weak disturbance moving across
the area through this evening, there will be some scattered light
showers north of Point Conception. With this shower activity, any
measurable rainfall should be only a few hundredths of an inch. 
For Saturday through Saturday night, dry conditions are expected.
However for Sunday through Monday morning time frame, a weak 
system will bring a decent chance of measurable rainfall to the 
area. At this time for the Sunday through Monday time frame,
rainfall totals are expected to be one quarter inch or less. With
these light totals, no hydrologic issues are expected.

Secondary "concern" for the short term will be winds, specifically
offshore winds tonight and Saturday. Latest models indicate the
LAX-DAG gradient bottoming out in the -2.0 to -3.5 MB range
tonight and Saturday morning. However, any upper level support is
forecast to be minimal. So, there will be some northeasterly 
winds tonight/Saturday morning in the usual northeast wind-prone
areas, but speeds are expected to remain below advisory levels.

As for temperatures, the weak offshore flow will allow for some
warming on Saturday, mainly west of the mountains, with highs
climbing into the mid to upper 60s. For Sunday and Monday, there
will be some minor day-to-day fluctuations in high temperatures.

.LONG TERM (TUE-FRI)...20/124 PM.

For the extended, models continue to exhibit good synoptic agreement
through the period. Main focus will be on a system moving across
the area in the Tuesday night through Wednesday night time frame.
Looking at both the deterministic and ensemble forecasts, this
system does not look too impressive at this time. For San Luis
Obispo and Santa Barbara counties, measurable rainfall looks
likely with totals of 0.10 to 0.50 inches expected (with higher
amounts around the Rocky Butte area). For Ventura and Los Angeles
counties, the chances of measurable rainfall are less and rainfall
totals, if any, would be around 0.10 inches or less. 

For Thanksgiving Day and Friday, dry conditions are expected as an
upper level ridge builds over the area and weak offshore flow
develops at the surface. High temperatures will top out in the mid
60s to mid 70s.

&&

.AVIATION...20/1744Z.

At 1712Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Overall, moderate to high confidence in 18Z TAF Package.
Timing of LIFR conditions may be off +/- 2 hours at KPRB.
15% chance of LIFR conditions at KSMX 21/12-16Z.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Westerly winds will shift
to the NW-N around 10 kts this evening. Weakening and turning
easterly after midnight with good confidence that east wind
component remains below 7 kts.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...20/803 AM.

Conditions across the coastal waters have significantly improved
from yesterday. However, conditions will remain hazardous to
small craft through tonight becoming relatively mild by Saturday.
A weak front will move across the coastal waters Sunday into 
Monday but minimal impacts are expected at this time. 

A stronger cold front is likely to impact the coastal waters
Tuesday night into Wednesday. Best chances for wind and rain
are likely to be off the Central coast due the front weakening 
on approach. Post-frontal low-end SCA level NW-W winds will 
still be possible Wednesday/night south of Point Conception. 
Large seas are also expected to return to the coastal waters 
around mid to late next week.

&&

.BEACHES...20/811 AM.

Elevated to high surf will create dangerous rip currents and 
beach conditions today. High Surf Advisories remain in effect for 
the Central Coast and Ventura Coast through 11 AM this morning, 
but even after that time strong rip currents are likely along most
westerly facing beaches. As swell height subsides, surf will 
gradually subside with relatively small surf for most beaches by 
Saturday. 

Extremely high tides, likely record breaking, will occur over
Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day). 
Additional large westerly swells are becoming increasingly likely
during the coming week as well. These swells have a good chance 
of producing a period of high surf for west facing beaches.

The combination of very high tides and increasing surf next week 
will likely lead to at least moderate-level, widespread coastal 
flooding issues across all coasts. There is potential for 
significant coastal flooding impacts if a larger swell overlaps 
with the timing of the extreme tides - that would likely occur
Wednesday and Thursday.
